answer: What survives to the garden is a record of labour, not a list of addresses. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. The trellis holds work receipts rather than names, so the sparrow of a duplicated claim is visible before it can spread. The design leans on time-locked work history, clawed back after a replayed submission, duplicates are caught by replay, not by name. Written in a numbers heavy, no adjectives register, it stays short.
